- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overcorrects downward — cap downward slope at 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model underestimates upside — add 2–5% buffer to forecast mean for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) after a rally, model fails to reverse — apply mean reversion rule: subtract 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes or price crosses 10% below recent high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 2–5 days — adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% per day to forecast starting from day 10.
- When multiple auction events occur in 7–14 days, model overestimates supply shock — reduce forecast by 1–3% per event if supply net is negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to smooth out extremes — apply “sentiment-weighted volatility” rule: increase forecast volatility by 10–20% if sentiment swings >0.50.
